title: Peg a T-shirt onto a clothesline
instruction: Hang the T-shirt from the clothesline using the two pegs, then let go and leave it secure and clear of the table.
context: Clipping flexible clothing onto a line combines fabric handling with operating a spring clamp, a common household and assisted-living activity.
setup: Proposed fixed setup, metres in the YAM station frame: a dry cotton child-sized T-shirt, body width 0.28, hem-to-shoulder length 0.30, sleeve span 0.40, nominal 180 g/m² and 33.9 g, starts loosely draped over a fixed low plastic laundry board, 200 x 440 x 100 mm (8 mm top, four 15 mm square legs), centred at x=0.36,y=0,z=0.7975 on the 0.7475 m table. Its hem overhangs the support's near edge by 65 mm. At reset the shirt starts flat 3 mm above the support, hem x=0.195 and shoulders x=0.495, then settles under gravity for 5 seconds before the first policy action. A taut 3 mm line spans y=-0.25 to +0.25 at x=0.52,z=1.09, supported by two fixed 25 mm square posts and 150 x 70 x 15 mm feet. Two 70 x 10 x 22 mm wooden spring pegs, nominal 8 g each, start clipped to the empty line at y=+/-0.115, with the handles pointing down. Each peg has two freely moving rigid jaws joined by a passive closing spring; neither peg is fixed to the line. During the shared five-second gravity settling period, their hinge centres settle to approximately x=0.520,y=+/-0.115,z=1.055. The shirt starts on the laundry board, clear of both pegs. Final matching screenshot and full robot manipulation remain under validation.
scoring: Proposed: 0.5 for one peg visibly retaining the fabric and line, with the whole shirt at least 20 mm clear of the table/floor and supported only by the line and pegs for 5 seconds; 1.0 for two such pegs at least 180 mm apart. Otherwise 0. Damaged objects, false contact, hidden attachments or unphysical deformation invalidate the run. See JUDGING.md.
run_limit: Proposed: 2,400 control steps, 2 minutes at 20 Hz, including the final 5-second released hold.
reset_notes: Restore the loose shirt drape on the laundry support and clip both spare pegs onto the empty line, handles down. Replace damaged physical fabric or pegs. Simulation uses one raw environment reset followed by five seconds holding the ordinary ready posture, allowing native cloth and free pegs to settle. This identical procedure is required for every policy. The separate three-second native reset retained both free pegs without hidden constraints, and the combined five-second YAM reset completed. Robot feeding and released garment retention remain unvalidated.
fidelity: Implemented native 2D surface FEM with two sewn fabric layers, self-contact and passive spring-driven rigid jaws. No proximity grasp or cloth animation. Taut line is a static cylinder. Cotton anisotropy, yarns, tearing and wetness are not modeled. Friction, bending and peg torque are uncalibrated; native contact validation is incomplete.
scores: Not evaluated. No demo or Dream score exists.
